description: Machine-readable editorial diagnostics for AI slop. Exact high-confidence constructions may block publication; lexical and structural signals require context.

hard_fail.rule: Use only for exact, high-confidence constructions in editable reader-facing copy. A hard-fail match blocks regardless of advisory score.

warn_if_repeated.rule: One occurrence may be intentional. Warn only when the category's repeat threshold is met.

contextual_review.rule: A match is a review prompt, not proof of bad writing. Check quotations, code, proper names, technical meanings, and surrounding evidence before editing.

structural_diagnostic.rule: Document-level heuristic. Diagnose in context and never add fragments, emotion, entities, or asymmetry merely to satisfy the detector.

broad_lexical_tells.description: Broad lexical tells. Never instant failures; review the meaning of each match in context.

connector_swaps.description: Possible simplifications. Replace only when the alternative preserves meaning and rhythm.

phrase_simplifications.description: Possible simplifications. Direct quotation, legal language, and technical wording may legitimately retain the original.

ai_tells.description: Common model-shaped phrases. Review in context; a single match is not a publication blocker.

retired_and_secret_reveal_constructions.description: Exact retired or secret-reveal framing. Remove from ordinary prose, but review quotations, titles under discussion, and literal reporting before editing.

production_commentary.description: Hard-fail production narration in captions, alt text, and reader-facing prose
notes: Patterns are verb-scoped or construction-scoped on purpose. Bare 'Playwright', 'Canva', 'ChatGPT', 'Midjourney', 'stock photo', 'screenshot', and 'prompt' are all legitimate subject matter on many sites, so only the production-narration constructions around them fail.

Internal tool or skill names that leak into captions (png-graphics, gpt-image, svg-graphics, annotated-screenshots) fail, but not when followed by a version number: gpt-image-2-2026-04-21 is a model id that legitimately appears in settings screenshots.
Validated against 8,226 real alt and caption strings from one production site: 0 false positives, and 31/31 on the production-narration test corpus.

'AI-generated' fails only when it qualifies the asset (image, illustration, graphic, render...) or stands alone as the whole caption. 'AI-generated keyword variations' describes a product feature and must pass.

asset_only_patterns hard-fail only in figcaption, img_alt, image_caption, and image_description. In body prose, list items, and table cells they are contextual_review: 'a landing page generated by an AI tool' or 'a comp created with Figma' can describe a reader's workflow rather than narrate this page's own production. The patterns that stay in `patterns` (fresh capture, not a generic mockup, real screenshot beats stock, render settings, prompt narration, leaked tool names) are production narration wherever they appear.

empty_intensifiers.description: Review these words for empty emphasis. Keep them when they carry literal scale, quotation, or necessary meaning.

hype_adjectives.description: Review these descriptors for unsupported hype. A quoted claim or proper name is not automatically a defect.

fancy_words.description: Possible plain-language substitutions. Preserve the original when it is the precise technical, mathematical, legal, or quoted term.

repeated_scaffolds.description: Rhetorical scaffolds that may carry one real turn but become model-shaped when repeated.

structural_patterns.description: Document-level diagnostics. Review the pattern and its cause; do not manufacture irregularity to make a metric pass.

checks.name: identical_paragraph_length
checks.description: All paragraphs within 10 words of each other

checks.name: symmetric_pros_cons
checks.description: Equal number of pros and cons with similar lengths

checks.name: uniform_sentence_band
checks.description: Nearly every sentence in a 2,000+ word piece falls in the same length band. Absence of fragments alone is not a defect; never add fragments solely to clear this diagnostic.

checks.name: dead_table_column
checks.description: A DATA column whose value is identical in every row (>=5 rows). Carries zero information; delete it and state the fact once in a sentence beside the table.
checks.exception: Action columns do not count: a column whose cells are all links or buttons ('Download', 'Try free', 'Sign Up') is a legitimate UI affordance and identical labels are expected. Prefer descriptive anchor text over 'Click here', but do not delete the column.

checks.name: near_dead_table_column
checks.description: A table column with the same value in >=80% of rows (>=5 rows). Usually collapsible into a note.

checks.name: repeated_per_item_sentence
checks.description: Same sentence closing 3+ item sections within one article

checks.name: sibling_article_boilerplate
checks.description: Section byte-identical across 3+ sibling articles in the same template family

checks.name: faq_duplicates_own_h2
checks.description: An FAQ entry restating one of the article's own H2 sections

checks.name: count_claim_mismatch
checks.description: Title or body claims N items but the article contains a different number

process_leakage.description: Exact tooling/apology constructions hard-fail. Compact claim boundaries are allowed; repeated scope disclaimers warn only after the configured threshold. Broad research terms remain contextual review.
patterns: \b(?:the (?:scraper|crawler|capture script|text browser|render(?:er)?) I (?:used|ran)|my (?:scraper|crawler|capture script)|the tool I used)\b
always_fail: \b(?:the (?:scraper|crawler|capture script|text browser|render(?:er)?) I (?:used|ran)|my (?:scraper|crawler|capture script)|the tool I used)\b
process_leakage.allowance: A claim boundary may be stated once, in the methodology or attached to the specific claim it bounds, phrased as a rule ('No tool receives an accuracy score unless it was queried under matching settings') or as a scope limit ('I have not run the same cloned checkout test, so I rank it on architecture, not an invented latency number'). That is correct practice, not a defect. A third limit_one occurrence, or per-item repetition, triggers warn_if_repeated review; it does not become a hard fail. always_fail contains only exact production/apology constructions.
notes: The scraper/crawler pattern is deliberately first-person-scoped: bare 'crawler'/'scraper' is legitimate SEO subject matter on many sites.

Bare 'text browser', 'Access reviewed', and 'no independently verified result' can carry legitimate technical or claim-boundary meaning, so they require contextual review rather than automatic blocking.

templated_filler.description: Sentences a roundup template emits identically for every item. Zero information about the item. The patterns are real examples from one site; add your own.
templated_filler.rule: If the same sentence closes 3+ item sections in one article, or is byte-identical across sibling articles, delete it. Advice true of every item belongs once, in the intro or buying section.
patterns: That makes the (?:book|tool|product|option) useful when your immediate goal matches
Read the table of contents and a sample chapter before buying
A clear sample at the right level is more valuable than
Check Amazon\.com or Amazon\.in for the exact edition
accepted_exceptions: A templated sentence may be kept when it carries a functional element such as the per-item links in a roundup. Record the exception in your own notes and do not add new instances.

scoring.scope: Advisory score for warn_if_repeated, contextual_review, and structural_diagnostic findings after human context review. Hard-fail matches are not scored; they block publication independently.
